correctness.rationale: All size-k committees are one-out replacements since there are k+1 candidates; score changes are p/(r+1)-q/k for C replacement, -h/r-q/k for A replacement. Every payment coalition is described exactly by three ballot-type counts; groups including q-type have a strictly larger-than-k/n witness; remaining coalitions have minimum maximum payment r/(p+h)+1/p. Necessary AM-GM inequality yields k>=r/(1-1/sqrt(r+1))^2 >=12. For all k>=12, r=2,p=6,h=10,q=2k+1 gives strict unique PAV optimality and an exact strong-EJR+ violation, with gap 1/984 at k=12. Core proof uses p*k/n<r+1. Exact rational checker was executed successfully.

value.rationale: A new proportionality axiom naturally raises a concrete compatibility question for the classical PAV rule. Strict uniqueness prevents a tie-breaking artifact; exact parameter conditions, core and EJR+ compatibility, and sharp 12-seat within-template obstruction explain why the payment criterion is stronger in a structured but natural shared-project versus bloc-choice approval market. The result includes an infinite family and an all-parameter analytic classification, not just a small numerical witness.
